name: Melatonin
short: Trial adverse events were few and mostly mild (daytime sleepiness, headache, dizziness); long-term data are limited. Drugs acting on CYP1A2 may slow its breakdown.
text: A systematic review of 37 placebo-controlled trials in sleep disorders found few, generally mild to moderate adverse events; the most frequent were daytime sleepiness, headache, dizziness and hypothermia, with no life-threatening events, though long-term evidence was scarce. A meta-analysis of higher-dose trials (10 mg or more), based on only four trials at low risk of bias, found no detectable increase in serious adverse events, but an increase in adverse events such as drowsiness, headache and dizziness; the authors describe the evidence as limited. Melatonin is broken down in the liver by CYP1A2, and a review notes that drugs interacting with CYP1A2 are likely to slow its metabolism.
